claim: Odd-year regular sessions begin on the Tuesday after the Martin Luther King, Jr. holiday
quote: In the case of an odd-numbered year regular session, on the Tuesday after the holiday for Martin Luther King, Jr.

claim: Even-year regular sessions begin on February 1, or the following Monday if February 1 falls Thursday to Sunday
quote: on the first day of February, except that if the first day of February is a Thursday, Friday, Saturday or Sunday, the regular session shall commence on the following Monday

claim: The Legislative Assembly holds annual sessions
quote: The Legislative Assembly shall hold annual sessions at the Capitol of the State.

claim: An odd-year session may not exceed 160 calendar days
quote: A session beginning in an odd-numbered year may not exceed 160 calendar days in duration

claim: An even-year session may not exceed 35 calendar days
quote: A session beginning in an even-numbered year may not exceed 35 calendar days in duration

claim: During the session the governor has five days, Saturdays and Sundays excepted, to return a bill or it becomes law
quote: If any bill shall not be returned by the Governor within five days (Saturdays and Sundays excepted) after it shall have been presented to the Governor, it shall be a law without signature

claim: After adjournment the governor has thirty days, Saturdays and Sundays excepted, to veto a bill; otherwise it becomes law
quote: unless the Governor within thirty days next after the adjournment (Saturdays and Sundays excepted) shall file such bill, with written objections thereto

claim: Acts take effect on January 1 of the year after passage unless the Act says otherwise
quote: Except as otherwise provided in the Act, an Act of the Legislative Assembly takes effect on January 1 of the year after passage of the Act.

claim: No act takes effect until ninety days after the session ends, except in an emergency
quote: No act shall take effect, until ninety days from the end of the session at which the same shall have been passed, except in case of emergency

claim: The general election is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each even-numbered year
quote: The general election shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each even-numbered year.

claim: The primary election is the third Tuesday in May of each even-numbered year
quote: The primary election shall be held on the third Tuesday in May of each even-numbered year.

claim: Major party candidates are nominated at the May primary for offices filled at the general election
quote: major political party candidates shall be nominated for offices to be filled at the general election held in that year

claim: All Oregon elections are conducted by mail
quote: County clerks shall conduct all elections in this state by mail.

claim: County offices and county-referred measures may only be on the March, May, August or November election dates, apart from emergency elections
quote: no election on a county measure referred by the county governing body or for a county office shall be held on any date other than

claim: City offices and council-referred measures may only be on the March, May, August or November election dates, apart from emergency elections
quote: no election on a city measure referred by the city governing body or for a city office shall be held on any date other than

claim: Cities must hold their nominating and regular elections for officers at the same time as the state primary and general elections
quote: Incorporated cities and towns shall hold their nominating and regular elections for their several elective officers at the same time that the primary and general biennial elections for State and county officers are held

claim: City charter election provisions stay in force except as to the time of holding elections
quote: pertaining to the holding of elections shall continue in full force and effect except so far as they relate to the time of holding

claim: All elections for city officers are held at the same time and place as state and county elections
quote: All elections for city officers shall be held at the same time and place as elections for state and county officers.

claim: A city may skip the May nominating election, in which case candidates file for the November election directly
quote: if a city does not hold a nominating election for municipal offices, a nominating petition or declaration of candidacy shall be filed not sooner than

claim: Special district boards, including school boards, are elected at the regular district election on the third Tuesday in May of each odd-numbered year
quote: The election shall be held in each such district in each odd-numbered year on the third Tuesday in May.

claim: A district may not hold more than one election of board members in a year
quote: A district shall not conduct more than one election of board members in any year.

claim: District board terms begin July 1 after the election
quote: The term of a board member elected at the regular district election shall commence on the first day of July next following the election

claim: A school district is a district for the purposes of the district election chapter
quote: (26) A school district.

claim: Rural fire protection districts are districts under the district election chapter
quote: A rural fire protection district organized under ORS chapter 478.

claim: Special elections called by a district are limited to the March, May, August and November dates, with a narrow exception for disaster repairs
quote: a special election called by a district elections authority shall not be held on any date other than

claim: District board candidates are nominated by petition or declaration of candidacy filed with the district elections officer, with no party route
quote: A candidate for election as a member of a district board shall be nominated by filing with the elections officer either

claim: School director elections are governed by the district election chapter
quote: The nomination and election of school directors.

claim: School directors are elected at the regular district election for four-year terms
quote: at each regular district election described in ORS 255.335, school directors shall be elected for a term of four years

claim: The term of a school director is four years
quote: The term of office of director is four years.

claim: School boards of districts under 300,000 people have five or seven members
quote: shall consist of five or seven members

claim: School directors are elected at large unless the board provides for zones
quote: all candidates shall be elected at large in the district unless the district school board provides for election from zones under ORS 332.126

claim: School, education service and community college districts may change their electoral system to comply with the Oregon voting rights provisions
quote: may authorize a change to the electoral system used by the qualifying district in order to comply with ORS 255.400 to 255.424

claim: Qualifying districts are school districts, education service districts and community college districts
quote: An education service district as defined in ORS 334.003

claim: Only voters registered with a major party may vote for that party's candidates at the primary, unless the party has opened its primary to nonaffiliated voters
quote: An elector is not qualified or permitted to vote at any primary election for any candidate of a major political party

claim: A major party may admit voters not affiliated with any party to its primary
quote: for a primary election that admits electors not affiliated with any political party

claim: A party member gets only their own party's primary ballot
quote: The elector may not be given a ballot of any other political party at that primary election.

claim: Nonaffiliated voters receive a primary ballot limited to the city, county and nonpartisan offices and measures they may vote on
quote: the county clerk shall mail to each elector who is not eligible to vote for party candidates a ballot limited to those offices and measures for which the elector is eligible to vote

claim: A candidate must have been a party member for at least 180 days before the filing deadline to receive that party's nomination
quote: If a candidate has not been a member of the major political party for at least 180 days before the deadline for filing

claim: A candidate who loses a major party primary may not run as another party's or a nonaffiliated candidate for the same office that November
quote: may not be the candidate of any other political party or a nonaffiliated candidate for the same office at the succeeding general election

claim: Statutory nonpartisan offices include county clerk, assessor, surveyor, treasurer, a county judge with judicial functions, sheriff, district attorney, and any office a home rule charter designates nonpartisan
quote: county clerk, county assessor, county surveyor, county treasurer, county judge who exercises judicial functions, sheriff, district attorney or any office designated nonpartisan by a home rule charter

claim: Justices of the peace and elected Metro offices are nonpartisan
quote: any elected office of a metropolitan service district under ORS chapter 268, justice of the peace

claim: County commissioner and a county judge without judicial functions can be partisan elective offices
quote: When a vacancy occurs in the partisan elective office of county judge who does not exercise judicial functions or county commissioner

claim: County commissioner and a county judge without judicial functions can also be nonpartisan offices
quote: when a vacancy occurs in the nonpartisan office of county judge who does not exercise judicial functions or county commissioner

claim: Nonpartisan candidates appear on the May nominating ballot without party designation
quote: shall be listed without political party designation on a nominating ballot

claim: Chapters 249 and 254 govern nominating and electing city officers in all cities
quote: This section and ORS chapters 249 and 254 govern the manner of nominating and electing candidates for municipal offices in all cities.

claim: State law leaves room for a party nomination for city office, recording the nominating party where applicable
quote: If applicable, the name of the major political party nominating the candidate.

claim: Candidates for nonpartisan office file a nominating petition or a declaration of candidacy
quote: An eligible elector may become a candidate for nonpartisan office, or for the nomination to an office by the major political party of which the elector is a member, by filing a nominating petition or a declaration of candidacy.

claim: The candidate with the most votes is nominated or elected
quote: When one person is to be nominated for or elected to an office, the person receiving the highest number of votes shall be nominated or elected.

claim: A nonpartisan candidate who wins a majority at the May nominating election is elected outright
quote: If a candidate for nonpartisan office receives a majority of votes cast for the office, that candidate is elected.

claim: Without a majority, the top two nonpartisan candidates in May advance to November
quote: Unless a candidate for nonpartisan office receives a majority of the votes cast for the office, the two candidates who receive the highest number of votes are nominated.

claim: The May majority rule for nonpartisan offices is subject to a home rule charter
quote: (2) The application of this section is subject to the provisions of a home rule charter. [1979 c.190

claim: With two or fewer candidates for sheriff, county treasurer or county clerk, they skip the May ballot and go straight to November
quote: The name or names of the candidate or candidates may not be printed on the ballot at the nominating election.

claim: With more than two candidates for sheriff, treasurer or clerk, a May majority makes that candidate the only nominee, not the winner
quote: If a candidate receives a majority of the votes cast for the office, that candidate alone is nominated.

claim: Minor parties, assemblies of electors and individual electors may each nominate one candidate per partisan office for the general election
quote: A minor political party, assembly of electors or individual electors may nominate one candidate for each partisan public office to be filled at the general election

claim: Any voter may sign a nonaffiliated candidate's petition or certificate of nomination
quote: A nominating petition or certificate of nomination of any nonaffiliated candidate

claim: Any voter may sign a nonpartisan candidate's nominating petition
quote: A nominating petition or certificate of nomination of any candidate for nonpartisan office

claim: A voter may sign nominating papers for more than one candidate for the same office
quote: Nominating petitions or certificates of nomination for more than one candidate for the same office.

claim: Only members of the candidate's own party may sign a major party candidate's nominating petition
quote: A person who is not a member of the same major political party as the candidate for nomination by the major political party may not sign the nominating petition of the candidate.

claim: ORS chapter 201 sets the boundaries of 36 counties, from Baker to Yamhill
quote: 201.360 Yamhill County. The boundary of Yamhill County is as follows

claim: Unless a charter provides otherwise, the county governing body is a county court of the county judge and two commissioners
quote: Unless otherwise provided by county charter, a county court shall be the governing body

claim: A county court consists of the county judge and two county commissioners
quote: shall consist of the county judge and two county commissioners

claim: A noncharter county whose county judge has no judicial function may replace the county judge with a third commissioner
quote: in which the county judge has no judicial function, may order the office of county judge abolished and create in lieu thereof a third county commissioner

claim: A board of county commissioners has three members unless a charter or ordinance provides otherwise
quote: Unless provided otherwise by county charter or ordinance, consist of three county commissioners.

claim: Counties elect a sheriff, county clerk, county assessor and county treasurer, and county commissioners
quote: The following county officers shall be elected at the primary election or general election

claim: The county surveyor is appointed unless a charter or ordinance provides otherwise
quote: Unless an adopted county charter or a county ordinance provides otherwise, the governing body of a county shall appoint a county surveyor.

claim: County officers serve four-year terms
quote: the term of office of each officer mentioned in ORS 204.005 is four years

claim: Each county commissioner seat is a numbered position
quote: each office of county commissioner shall be designated by number as Position No. 1, Position No. 2 or Position No. 3

claim: A county charter prescribes the organization of county government, including the number, election or appointment and tenure of officers
quote: A county charter shall prescribe the organization of the county government and shall provide directly, or by its authority, for the number, election or appointment, qualifications, tenure, compensation, powers and duties of such officers as the county deems necessary.

claim: A county charter cannot change how judges, justices of the peace or district attorneys are selected
quote: a county charter shall not affect the selection, tenure, compensation, powers or duties prescribed by law for judges in their judicial capacity, for justices of the peace or for district attorneys

claim: County voters adopt, amend or repeal a charter by majority vote
quote: by majority vote of such electors voting on the question at any legally called election, may adopt, amend, revise or repeal a county charter

claim: The voters of every city and town may enact and amend their own charter
quote: The legal voters of every city and town are hereby granted power to enact and amend their municipal charter

claim: The Legislature may not enact or amend a city charter
quote: The Legislative Assembly shall not enact, amend or repeal any charter or act of incorporation for any municipality, city or town.

claim: A city incorporated under the general law has five councillors by default
quote: shall be five councillors, a municipal judge and such other officers as the council deems necessary

claim: In a general-law city, three councillors are elected every two years
quote: Three councillors shall be elected biennially.

claim: In a general-law city, the council chooses the mayor from among its members
quote: The council shall appoint a mayor at its first meeting of each odd-numbered year.

claim: City charters are adopted, amended or repealed by simple majority vote
quote: the adoption, amendment, revision, repeal or surrender of a city charter shall be decided by simple majority vote

claim: State election law governs the conduct of all city elections
quote: ORS chapters 246 to 260 govern the conduct of all city elections.

claim: A charter or ordinance may set the manner of filing for city office
quote: If the city charter or ordinance provides a manner of filing for nomination, a candidate for any office of that city shall file in that manner.

claim: Portland elects its councilors, mayor and auditor at the general election using ranked choice voting
quote: City Councilors, the Mayor and the Auditor are elected in the general election, except as otherwise provided in this Charter, using ranked choice voting.

claim: Portland elects its mayor and auditor by instant runoff
quote: The Mayor and the Auditor are elected at-large using a method of ranked choice voting known as instant runoff voting.

claim: Portland elects district councilors by single transferable vote
quote: Councilors of each district are elected using a proportional method of ranked choice voting known as single transferable vote.

claim: Portland has four council districts with three councilors each
quote: There are four (4) City Council districts. Each district is represented by three (3) City Councilors

claim: Portland city offices are nonpartisan
quote: The elective offices of City Councilors, the Mayor and the Auditor are nonpartisan.

claim: Portland officers serve four-year terms
quote: those elected take office on the January 1 following the general election in which they are elected and hold office for four years

claim: Portland charter election changes were adopted by voters on November 8, 2022
quote: [Section replaced November 8, 2022, effective December 14, 2022.]
